item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Car Photo in Black and White

turns.text: Make this black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it.

item.tests: Converts the supplied photo to neutral grayscale without regenerating, rearranging or cropping its contents.

answer_sheet.Black-and-white treatment: Neutral grayscale across the whole photo, not sepia or selective colour.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Everything except colour, including the car, street, background and full original framing.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One image in the original shape of the photo (5:3); free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The entire image is neutral black and white, with no red remaining on the car or colour elsewhere.
The same compact hatchback remains in the same position and has unchanged body details.
The street and background objects retain their original positions and appearance apart from colour.
The full original composition is retained without cropping, in the photo's own shape.

turns.text: Make this pic black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
For **only removing colour with no crop or other changes**, a standard grayscale filter is the best option—and it can cost **0 Magic Hour credits**.

- **Free method:** Open the original in your phone or computer’s photo editor, set **Saturation to −100 (or 0, depending on the app)**, and save a copy. Leave cropping, resizing, and auto-enhance off.
- **Magic Hour:** The lowest listed AI-editing price is **5 credits for one image using Flux 2 Klein at 640px**. It’s a generative edit, so it could alter details rather than simply remove colour. I wouldn’t recommend it for your exact-preservation requirement.

“Shorter” doesn’t apply to a still photo, and a smaller image won’t reduce that listed minimum.

**I haven’t started an edit or spent any credits.** Tell me your device or photo app and I can give you the exact free steps.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that free grayscale option—just remove the colour and preserve everything else, including the full original framing.

dialog.agent:
Sorry—I should have clarified: I can guide you through the free option, but I don’t have a non-generative grayscale tool here to apply it directly. **No credits have been spent.**

To preserve all details and the full framing, open the original in a photo editor, set **Saturation to its minimum**, and save a copy at the **original dimensions**. Keep crop, resize, filters, and auto-enhance off.

Which device or photo app are you using? I’ll give you the exact steps.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the edit because your account doesn’t have enough credits for the **5-credit option**. **No image was generated and no credits were spent.**

The zero-credit alternative is still to reduce saturation to its minimum in a standard photo editor, leaving crop and resize untouched.
